provenance: Seeded by construction on 2026-10-01. Every page otherwise meets the deterministic floor, so deterministic detections that match no defect here are false positives. EVALUATION-PLAN §3 asks for two independent labellers on analytical defects; that review has not happened yet, so the cw stories and severity bands are the seeder's analytical judgement.

defects.description: The only way back to the dates from the berth list is a Change dates link inside an unlabelled three-dot More options menu. A skipper who needs another arrival day sees no date control and no visible link, so they are unlikely to notice that the action exists.

cw.question: CW-Q2
cw.failure_story: The skipper looks for the dates on the berth list and finds only the stay summary sentence. Nothing labelled with dates is visible; the three-dot button gives no hint that it holds Change dates, so they press Back or start again.

defects.description: No step indicator anywhere in the four-step booking: no step count, no list of steps and no back link between steps, so the skipper cannot tell how far through the booking they are or how much remains.

The boat-details field is labelled only Length: it does not say length overall including bowsprit and davits, which is what the berth limits use, nor the unit. Skippers commonly know both hull length and length overall, and may enter the shorter hull length or a value in feet.

cw.question: CW-Q3
cw.failure_story: The skipper knows 9.6 metres on the hull and 10.4 metres overall. The label says only Length, so they may type 9.6, and the booking then accepts a berth the boat does not fit.

defects.description: When the length entered is over the chosen berth's limit, the page replaces the form with Booking stopped and a bare reference (BK-409). It does not say what went wrong, keeps no entered data, and offers no way to correct the length or choose a longer berth: a dead end.

The tide table gives high water only in UTC, while the arrival-time list and the harbour office work in local time (British Summer Time in October). Skippers who plan from this table are an hour out for the sill gate.

Berth prices are shown only per metre per night, and the boat length is asked for later, so the skipper has to work out and remember each total to compare berths; the total first appears on the review page.
Going back from the review page with the browser's Back button empties every boat detail (the page resets the form on pageshow), so correcting one value means typing all of them again.

One thing has three names through the flow: visitor berth on the first page, pontoon space on the berth list, and mooring on the review page, so skippers cannot tell whether they are booking the same thing.

The arrival-time list offers every hour from 06:00 to 21:00 and accepts times when the sill gate is closed, with no warning; the gate rule appears only as a note under the tide table further down the page.
The boat page requires an MMSI with no explanation of the abbreviation, where to find it, or what to do if the boat's radio has none; the error message only repeats Enter the MMSI.

cw.question: CW-Q3
cw.failure_story: This skipper has an MMSI on the radio, but nothing on the page connects the label MMSI with the nine-digit radio identity; skippers whose radio has no MMSI have no way forward at all.

defects.description: The confirmation gives a reference but no arrival instructions: not the sill-gate window for the booked day, the VHF channel to call on approach, or where to find the visitor pontoon.
